# Fire's parts (192, Fire 0.14.1)

One line for every component, pattern, layout, website section and module: its id, where it is used, and its job.
Search first (`fire find "<what it does>"`); read the family here when the search gives nothing close, because the
part may exist under a name you did not try. Then read the part's card in `contract/catalog.json` (when to use it and
what to use instead) and copy its markup from the docs section the card names. An id is not a class:
`docs/_ref/CLASSES.md` lists every class.

## Agent

- `agent` (pattern; app): Lay out a whole agent screen: past sessions, the thread and a docked composer.
- `approval-bar` (app): Ask whether the agent may run an action, with allow once, always allow and deny.
- `composer` (app, phone): Ask the agent for something and attach context, sources and a model.
- `message` (app, phone): Show one turn of an agent conversation: the person in a bubble, the agent in prose.
- `playground` (pattern; app): Try one capability of a data source with a request form and a response panel.
- `reasoning` (app, phone): Fold away the plan behind an answer for the person who wants to check it.
- `result` (app): Show the data an agent returned as a table, with a JSON view and a cost line.
- `run-steps` (app): Show the plan of a long run and tick it off as it goes.
- `session-list` (app): Pick up an earlier agent session, or start a new one.
- `sources` (app, phone): Show where an answer came from, with numbered citations and a list of sources.
- `suggestions` (app, phone): Offer example prompts that fill the composer when clicked.
- `thread` (app, phone): Hold the turns of an agent conversation in order.
- `toolcall` (app): Show one step the agent took, with its arguments, time and cost.
- `use-agent` (app, website): Offer to add the product to the person's own agent or coding tool.

## Base

- `divider` (app, website, phone): Separate two groups with a hairline.
- `icon` (app, website, phone): Draw a small symbol beside a label or on a button.
- `inline-code` (app, website, phone): Mark a command, a path or a key inside a sentence.
- `text` (app, website, phone): Change the tone or length of a piece of text.
- `type` (app, website, phone): Set the size and weight of a heading, label or body text.
- `utilities` (app, website, phone): Hide text from sight but keep it for screen readers, or add a small motion.

## Buttons

- `button` (app, website, phone): Start an action or confirm a choice with one press.
- `fab` (app, website, phone): Keep one primary action in reach while the page scrolls.

## Charts

- `bars` (app, website): Rank items by size: credits by endpoint, requests by key.
- `chart` (app, website): See how values change over time or between periods.
- `donut` (app, website): Show parts of a whole, or one value against a known end.
- `heatgrid` (app, website): See activity over weeks, one cell per day, or an outcome per day.
- `legend` (app, website): Say which colour means which series.
- `sparkline` (app, website): Show the direction of a number in a few pixels beside it.

## Chat

- `chat` (app, website, phone): Talk with an AI assistant and a support person in one thread, with rich replies.
- `chat-launcher` (app, website, phone): Open and close the chat from a floating button with an unread count.
- `chat-lightbox` (app, website, phone): View a chat image full size and step through the others.
- `chat-message` (app, website, phone): Show who said what in a chat, and carry blocks such as forms, cards and approvals.

## Code

- `codeblock` (app, website): Show code a developer will read or paste, with copy, line numbers and language tabs.
- `diff` (app, website): Show what a change does before it is saved.
- `endpoint` (app, website): Name an API call by its method and path wherever it appears.
- `json` (app, website): Explore a JSON response by folding it, not by reading it whole.
- `log` (app, website): Watch a stream of lines and search them without losing your place.
- `schema` (app, website): Document the parameters of an endpoint: names, types, defaults and nested fields.
- `snippet` (app, website): Copy one command or one value, or follow a short list of numbered commands.
- `viewswitch` (app, website): Switch the same data between two views, such as a table and its JSON.

## Content

- `accordion` (app, website, phone): Show and hide sections of text so a long page stays short.
- `announce` (app, website): Mark a launch or milestone with one full-width accent panel.
- `avatar` (app, website, phone): Show who or what something belongs to with initials or a picture.
- `badge` (app, website, phone): Label something with a short word or a count.
- `banner` (app, website): Tell the whole account something once, in a strip under the top bar.
- `callout` (app, website, phone): Tell the reader what happened and what to do, next to the content it is about.
- `card` (app, website, phone): Group the parts of one object on a quiet surface.
- `commit` (app, website, phone): Take a reason and commit a decision with buttons named for their effect.
- `decision` (app, website, phone): Show what a decision changes, who it touches, the evidence and who signs, so a person can decide in seconds.
- `delta` (app, website, phone): Show a value before and after a change, with an arrow between them.
- `draft` (app, phone): Offer words an agent wrote for a person, which stay the agent's until the person uses them.
- `empty` (app, website, phone): Say what will appear here and give the one action that fills it.
- `feature-list` (app, website): List what a plan or product includes, one line each with an icon.
- `hold` (app, phone): Wait a few seconds before an action goes, with a countdown and Undo.
- `impact` (app, phone): Say how much a change will touch, before anyone commits it.
- `plan` (app, website): Show a pricing plan as a row in billing or a card in a pricing grid.
- `preview` (pattern; app): Edit a value, see what the change will touch, then commit it with a reason.
- `qr` (app, website): Let someone scan a code with a phone to pair a device or add an authenticator.
- `queue` (pattern; app, phone): Work through what waits for a decision, one case at a time, beside the list.
- `scroller` (app, website, phone): Scroll a row of cards sideways with snapping and arrows.
- `setting` (app, phone): Put one setting on a row: what it is on the left, its control on the right.
- `states` (pattern; app, website, phone): Show the one state a screen or a section is in: loading, ready, empty, error, no access and the rest.
- `status` (app, website, phone): Show the state of a run, a monitor or a key with a dot and a word.
- `tag` (app, website, phone): Mark or filter something by category with a small pill.
- `thumb` (app, website, phone): Show a small picture of a record, such as a video's poster frame, cropped to a fixed shape.
- `tile` (app, website, phone): Hold a logo, a glyph or one or two letters in a square.
- `timeline` (app, website): Read the history of one thing as a list of events in time order.
- `verified` (app, website): Show that an account or a provider has been verified.

## Data

- `confirm-row` (app, phone): Ask in an item's own row whether to remove, revoke or sign it out, before the action runs.
- `data-card` (app): Show one figure with its context and keep the detail one click away.
- `filter` (app): Narrow a table or a list by one value, shown as a chip that opens a menu.
- `filters` (app, phone): Narrow a table or list by many fields from one Filter button, and see each filter that is set as a chip.
- `kv` (app, website, phone): Read what an object is as labelled values in a grid.
- `list` (app, website, phone): Show rows that are mostly text with one action each.
- `list-detail` (app, phone): Work through a queue: pick a record from a list and read or act on it beside the list.
- `meter` (app, website): Show how much of a limit is used.
- `pipeline` (app): See what ran, what runs in parallel and what comes after, for one run.
- `progress` (app, website, phone): Show work moving to done: a crawl, an import, a run.
- `stats` (app, website): Read a few headline numbers at a glance, as one joined strip.
- `table` (app, website, phone): Compare, sort and act on records laid out in rows and columns.

## Documentation

- `doc` (website, phone): Build a documentation site in the product's own look: nav, article, contents and footer.
- `doc-ask` (website): Point readers to the assistant at the end of a docs section.
- `doc-cards` (website): Fan out from an overview to the pages beneath it with link cards.
- `doc-changelog` (website): List dated releases on a rail with filters by kind or area.
- `doc-endpoint` (website): Document an API endpoint: parameters on the left, request and response on the right.
- `doc-frame` (app, website, phone): Show a screenshot, video, diagram or a supplied picture in a captioned frame that can open larger.
- `doc-setup` (website): Get a reader connected by choosing their tool, with the steps for it below.
- `doc-steps` (website): Follow a setup in order, one numbered step at a time, each with its prose and code.
- `prose` (app, website): Style rendered Markdown or long text without adding classes.

## Forms

- `checkbox` (app, website, phone): Tick one or more options, or a yes that saves with the form.
- `choice` (app, website, phone): Choose from options that each need a title and a sentence.
- `codefield` (app, website): Edit raw code or JSON that has to be valid.
- `codes` (app, website): Show one-time recovery codes once, with copy and download.
- `color` (app): Enter a colour with a picker or a hex code and see how it reads on the page.
- `combobox` (app, website, phone): Pick from a long list by typing to filter it.
- `confirm-inline` (app): Make someone type a name on the page before a destructive button works.
- `copy-field` (app, website, phone): Show a value people copy, such as an address or an ID.
- `datefield` (app, website): Enter one date by typing it or picking it from a calendar.
- `field` (app, website, phone): Give a control a label, a hint and room for one error.
- `file-upload` (app, website): Add files by dropping them or browsing; one image as a settings row for a logo.
- `form` (app, website, phone): Lay out fields and actions in a form that stays readable.
- `form-section` (pattern; app, website, phone): Group the fields of a long form under a title.
- `input` (app, website, phone): Type one line of text, a URL, a key or a number.
- `input-group` (app, website, phone): Put an icon, prefix, unit or button inside one field.
- `listbox` (app, website, phone): Show a list of options a person can choose from.
- `matrix` (app, website): Set one switch for each category and channel in a grid.
- `number` (app, website, phone): Enter a number and nudge it up or down.
- `otp` (app, website, phone): Enter a short code from a message or an app.
- `pairs` (app, website): Edit a set of names with values as rows.
- `radio` (app, website, phone): Choose exactly one option from a few.
- `reason` (app): Show why a control is off and who can turn it on.
- `search` (app, website, phone): Search a list or a page by typing.
- `secret` (app, website): Show or enter a secret that stays masked until asked.
- `select` (app, website, phone): Choose one option from a list in a native menu.
- `slider` (app, website, phone): Pick a position on a scale by dragging.
- `swatch` (app, website): Show a colour that is content, such as a brand colour or a series colour.
- `switch` (app, website, phone): Turn a setting on or off, with the change applying at once.
- `tag-input` (app, website, phone): Enter a free-form list of values, one token each.
- `textarea` (app, website, phone): Write an answer that runs over several lines.

## Layout

- `column` (layout; app, website, phone): Keep a narrow block readable on a wide page.
- `grid` (layout; app, website, phone): Lay out equal columns that fill the width and reflow.
- `grow` (layout; app, website, phone): Let one child take the space left over in a row.
- `row` (layout; app, website, phone): Put things side by side with even space.
- `stack` (layout; app, website, phone): Put things one above another with even space.

## Modules

- `email` (module; email): Send a sign-in link, receipt, alert or newsletter issue as an email that matches the product.
- `initial-helpers` (module; app, website, email): Draw an organisation's first-letter mark on a server or in an email, with no DOM.
- `theme-record` (module; app, website, email): Turn a product's whole look, one JSON record, into tokens, a stylesheet or a palette.
- `transitions` (module; app, website, phone): Move from one page to the next with the chrome held still and only the content changing.

## Navigation

- `back` (app, website, phone): Return to the one obvious previous place.
- `breadcrumb` (app, website): Show where this screen sits and jump to a parent.
- `chip-nav` (app, website, phone): Browse a catalogue by category.
- `pagination` (app, website): Move through a list that is split into pages.
- `segmented` (app, website, phone): Pick one of two to five options that change what you see here.
- `skip` (app, website, phone): Skip past the header and the navigation to the page's content in one key press.
- `steps` (app, website, phone): Show where someone is in a flow with a fixed order, or how far live work or a record has got.
- `subnav` (app, website, phone): Move between settings pages from a side column.
- `tabs` (app, website, phone): Switch between views of the same object.
- `toc` (website): List the sections of a long page and follow the reader.

## Overlays

- `checklist` (app, phone): Pick several values from a long list, with search and counts.
- `command` (app, website): Jump to a page or run an action by typing, from anywhere.
- `confirm` (app): Make someone type a name before a destructive action runs.
- `date-picker` (app): Choose a start and an end date, with presets for the usual ranges.
- `dialog` (app, website, phone): Stop the page until the person finishes or dismisses one task.
- `hovercard` (app, website): Preview a link's target, such as a person or a provider, without leaving the page.
- `menu` (app, website, phone): Pick an action or a choice from a short list that belongs to one trigger.
- `notification` (app, phone): Read the list of things that happened, with the unread ones marked.
- `period` (app): Choose a reporting period and what to compare it with.
- `popover` (app, website, phone): Show richer content than a list next to its trigger: a summary, a small form, a picker.
- `sheet` (app, website, phone): Show the detail of something picked from a list without losing the list.
- `toast` (app, website, phone): Confirm something that already happened, then get out of the way.
- `tooltip` (app, website): Name an icon-only control or reveal its shortcut on hover or focus.

## Shell

- `app` (app, phone): Frame every signed-in screen with a sidebar, a top bar and a page.
- `brand` (app, website, phone): Sign a surface with the product mark and name, an uploaded logo or a wordmark.
- `initial` (app, website): Show an organisation's first letter as a dot-matrix mark where it has no logo.
- `mobile-nav` (app, phone): Open the full navigation as a sheet on a phone.
- `page` (app, website): Lay a page out as a drafted column cut into bands by hairlines.
- `page-head` (app): Title a working page and put its actions at the end of the row.
- `page-hero` (app, website): Open a top-level screen with a tall title band and one line about it.
- `panel` (app, website): Hold a titled group of content, or a 320px pane of sessions beside the rail.
- `running` (app): Show how many jobs are in progress and open the list from the top bar.
- `screen` (pattern; app, website, phone): Centre one task on a page of its own, outside the shell.
- `service-status` (app, website): Show whether the product is healthy: an icon when normal, a labelled pill when not.
- `shortcuts` (app): Go to a page by keyboard and list every shortcut in a sheet.
- `sidebar` (app): Move between the product's sections from a list on the left.
- `split` (app, website): Put details beside the thing they describe, in two columns.
- `tabbar` (app, phone): Put three to five main destinations one thumb-press away at the bottom of a phone.
- `toolbar` (app, website): Search, filter and act on a list, with controls wrapping instead of scrolling.
- `topbar` (app, phone): Switch teams, reach help and docs, and take the one primary action.

## Texture & loading

- `loader` (app, website, phone): Show that something small is loading with a ring, dots, bars or a text frame.
- `pagebar` (app, website): Show that a page is navigating or reloading with a thin bar at the top.
- `skeleton` (app, website, phone): Hold a place for content that is loading, with the same shape as the real thing.
- `texture` (app, website): Add a quiet generated field of characters, dots or marks behind a hero, banner or empty state.

## Tweaks

- `tweaks` (app, website): Change the whole look of the product live: palette, type, tone, density, corners and motion.

## Website

- `site` (pattern; website): Hold a public page and give every section on it the same breakpoints, type steps, rhythm and grounds.
- `site-article` (website section; website): Read a post, report or paper at reading length, with its sources and notes.
- `site-compare` (website section; website): Compare plans or products feature by feature in a table, one column at a time on a phone.
- `site-container` (pattern; website): Keep a section's content on one line of 1,200px, a 720px reading column, or the full width.
- `site-cta` (website section; website): Ask for the one next step near the end of a page: a band, an inset panel, or a title beside a one-field form.
- `site-faq` (website section; website): Answer the questions people ask before they buy, in an accordion or in open columns.
- `site-features` (website section; website): Explain what the product does as a few parts, ruled cells, editorial rows or one large part with smaller ones.
- `site-footer` (website section; website): End every public page with link columns, the legal line and the service status.
- `site-head` (pattern; website): Open a website section with an eyebrow, a title, a lead line and its actions.
- `site-header` (website section; website): Show the brand, the main links and the sign-up action at the top of every public page.
- `site-hero` (website section; website): State what the product does on the first screen, with one primary action and one line of proof.
- `site-logos` (website section; website): Show which companies use the product, as wordmarks in the text colour.
- `site-media` (website): Show a site's own photograph in a section, cropped to a set shape and treated by the look.
- `site-posts` (website section; website): List posts, releases or resources as rows, cards or one lead entry, filtered and paged.
- `site-pricing` (website section; website): Show what each plan costs and includes, with a monthly or yearly switch.
- `site-quote` (website section; website): Show what customers said, with their name, role and company.
- `site-split` (website section; website): Make one claim beside one piece of media, with a ruled list of points under it.
- `site-stats` (website section; website): Prove a claim with three or four large figures and what each one counts.
- `site-steps` (website section; website): Show how to start in three or four ordered steps, as columns or as a rail with code beside each.
